name: Andaman Islands
tagline: Coral seas, white sands and dense tropical island calm.
bestMonths: Jan, Feb, Mar, Nov and Dec
whenBlurb: Come in the dry season, November to April, for calm seas and clear diving; time it to turtle nesting December-March or the January Island Tourism Festival, and avoid the May-to-September monsoon.

ourTake.lede: The Andamans are about the water and a small number of exceptional beaches, not a packed island-hopping schedule, so pick one or two islands and stay put rather than churning through ferries. Havelock (Swaraj Dweep) has the famous sand and diving; Neil (Shaheed Dweep) is the quieter one. Do the diving or snorkelling properly with a good operator, and treat the historical Cellular Jail in Port Blair as a meaningful half-day, not an afterthought.
ourTake.comeIf: You want white sand and clear water without leaving the country or arranging a visa.
ourTake.skipIf: You want cities, culture or nightlife.

guide.lede: Where to stay, what to do, where to eat, and where the night goes, grouped by price, every address earned by a name worth trusting.

items.name: Taj Exotica Resort & Spa, Andamans
credentials: Taj Hotels (IHCL) flagship luxury resort, the Andamans' only internationally-branded five-star
Set on Radhanagar Beach, long ranked among Asia's finest (TIME, 'Best Beach in Asia', 2004)
items.description: Seventy-two thatched villas on stilts across 46 acres of rainforest above Radhanagar, the one true icon of the islands, and reason enough to make the crossing.

items.name: Jalakara
credentials: Condé Nast Traveller, Gold List 2020 ("by far the loveliest place to stay" in the Andamans)
Mr & Mrs Smith, personally-visited member hotel
items.description: Seven singular rooms hidden in virgin rainforest on a hillside inland, a British-built jungle villa-hotel that feels wholly private and quietly perfect.

items.name: Barefoot at Havelock
credentials: The first sustainably designed and operated resort in the Andamans (eco-pioneer standing)
Closest quality stay to Radhanagar Beach
items.description: The resort that opened Havelock in 2002, Nicobari-inspired cottages of cane, thatch and wood in 25 acres of forest, a hundred metres from Radhanagar.

items.name: Symphony Palms Beach Resort & Spa
credentials: Official five-star beach resort, Havelock, among the island's largest full-service properties
Extensive in-house dive centre and water-sports operation
items.description: A large, capable five-star on Govind Nagar beach, sunrise views, an ocean spa and beach candlelight dinners, run at scale.

items.name: Sea Shell Resort & Spa, Havelock
credentials: Sea Shell Group, one of the longest-running quality hotel operators across the Andamans (Havelock, Neil and Port Blair)
items.description: A well-established seaside chalet resort with a spa, a dependable, comfortable Havelock stay close to the jetty and the beaches.

items.name: Sea Shell, Neil
credentials: Sea Shell Group, Neil Island's leading quality resort
items.description: The most comfortable base on quiet Neil, the slow, uncrowded island for members who want stillness over scene.

items.name: The Cellular Jail National Memorial, the Kala Pani
items.description: The colonial 'Kala Pani' prison where Veer Savarkar and hundreds of freedom fighters were exiled and tortured, seven radiating wings of solitary cells built so no prisoner could see or signal another. For an Indian family this is not sightseeing but pilgrimage; walk the surviving three wings, stand in Savarkar's cell, and let the gallows and the flogging yard land in silence.

items.name: The Light-and-Sound Show at the Cellular Jail
items.description: As dusk falls over the prison courtyard, an old peepal tree 'narrates' the story of the jail across forty-five minutes of light, music and voice, the most moving hour on the islands and best in the original Hindi. Have your advisor book the front rows; younger children and grandparents alike leave shaken and proud.

items.name: Radhanagar Beach (Beach No. 7) at sunset
credentials: Ranked 'Best Beach in Asia' by TIME magazine (2004); among the world's top-rated beaches
Blue Flag–certified beach
items.description: A kilometre of powder-white sand backed by rainforest and lapped by glass-clear turquoise, routinely called one of Asia's finest beaches and the postcard image of the Andamans. Come for the late afternoon when day-trippers thin out, wade into the warm shallows, and watch the sun drop straight into the Bay of Bengal.

items.name: Scuba diving the Havelock reefs, Nemo Reef & Barracuda City
items.description: Havelock is India's premier dive base, twenty-plus sites with soft and hard coral gardens, 20–30m visibility in season, and reliable sightings of turtles, rays, reef sharks and clouds of fish. Gentle sites like Nemo Reef and Barracuda City suit first dives and children over ten, while PADI 5-Star centres certify you from Discover-Scuba to Open Water in a few unhurried days.

items.name: Snorkelling & the coral gardens of Elephant Beach
items.description: Reached by a short boat hop or a forest walk, Elephant Beach has live coral just off the sand, the easiest, most rewarding snorkel on Havelock, with guides holding your hand in shin-deep water if needed. It is the family water-sports hub too: glass-bottom boats, sea-walking and jet-skis, so non-swimmers and teenagers are equally occupied.

items.name: Kalapathar Beach at sunrise
items.description: Named for the black rocks that punctuate its white sand, this quiet east-facing crescent is where you watch the first light spill over the sea while most of the island still sleeps. A short, contemplative stop with a coffee flask, beautiful, uncrowded and photogenic in the low morning sun.

items.name: Vijaynagar Beach (Beach No. 5) morning walk
items.description: The long, tree-lined stretch fronting Havelock's older resorts, shallow, calm and famous for its sunrise, a short walk from Kalapathar. One of the island's genuinely peaceful corners for an early stroll before the day's activities begin.

items.name: Bioluminescence & mangrove night kayaking
items.description: On a moonless night you paddle silent creeks where every stroke ignites the water into blue-green sparks, dinoflagellates that glow at the touch. Led by a guide in a stable double kayak, it needs no paddling experience and is the single most magical thing couples and families do here; the darker the moon, the brighter the sea.

items.name: Game fishing charter off Havelock
items.description: The reefs, drop-offs and channels minutes from Havelock are world-class sport-fishing grounds, popping and jigging for giant trevally, and trolling for sailfish, wahoo and tuna in the December-to-February peak. Private AC charters run catch-and-release with professional crews; a marquee half- or full-day for the anglers in a multi-generational group.

items.name: Private-boat island-hopping & sunset cruise
items.description: Charter a speedboat, catamaran or small yacht and string together the quiet corners, a snorkel stop, a deserted sandbar, a beach picnic, Neil Island, entirely on your own clock, skipping the public-ferry crush. A sunset cruise off Havelock, with the crew laying on drinks and privacy, is the natural centrepiece for an anniversary or honeymoon.

items.name: Ross Island (Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose Dweep), the ruins
items.description: A fifteen-minute boat from Aberdeen Jetty lands you on the old British capital, once the 'Paris of the East', now a haunting garden of ballrooms, a church and a bakery being swallowed whole by strangler-fig roots. Netaji hoisted the tricolour here in 1943; deer and peacocks now wander the colonial bones, making it the islands' most atmospheric short excursion.

items.name: North Bay Island, sea-walking & snorkelling
items.description: The reef pictured on the ₹20 note sits just off North Bay, and here even non-swimmers can 'sea-walk' the seabed inside a fed-air helmet, entirely dry-haired and calm. Snorkelling, glass-bottom boats and scuba round it out, the ideal soft introduction to the underwater Andamans on your first day out of Port Blair.

items.name: Corbyn's Cove Beach
items.description: Port Blair's own coconut-fringed town beach, a short drive from the jetty and lined with palms, an easy sunset-and-a-drink stop when you are based in the capital rather than a swim-all-day destination. Convenient, relaxed and pleasantly close to the airport for the first or last afternoon of a trip.

items.name: Samudrika Naval Marine Museum
items.description: Run by the Indian Navy, this well-kept museum walks you through the islands' geography, tribes and reef ecology, with a small aquarium and the skeleton of a blue whale washed ashore in Nicobar. A cool, air-conditioned hour that sets up everything you will later see underwater, good for curious children before a snorkelling day.

items.name: Anthropological Museum
items.description: A thoughtful, small museum on the indigenous peoples of the archipelago, the Great Andamanese, Onge, Jarawa and the uncontacted Sentinelese, with tools, dwellings and photographs that give respectful context to communities whose reserves are rightly off-limits. The quiet, essential grounding for understanding these islands beyond their beaches.

items.name: Chatham Saw Mill & Forest Museum
items.description: On a small island linked to Port Blair by a bridge, one of Asia's oldest sawmills still cuts island timber, with a forest museum of carved teak and padauk and a war-scarred bomb pit from the Japanese occupation. A short, offbeat stop for those drawn to industrial and wartime history.

items.name: Chidiya Tapu, sunset point & Munda Pahad trek
items.description: The southern tip of South Andaman, a short drive from town, where the mangroves and birdlife give way to the best sunset near Port Blair. A gentle trek up Munda Pahad opens panoramic sea views on both sides, a rewarding late-afternoon escape without leaving the main island.

items.name: Mount Harriet National Park (Mount Manipur)
items.description: The highest hill on South Andaman, wrapped in tropical forest and butterflies, with a lookout over the harbour and Ross Island, the very view once engraved on the ₹20 note. A cool, green half-day drive-and-walk for those who want forest and vantage over sand.

items.name: The Natural Bridge (Howrah Bridge), Neil Island
items.description: A wave-carved coral-rock arch beside Laxmanpur, reachable on foot only at low tide across pools full of starfish, sea cucumbers and small fish, locals nicknamed it the 'Howrah Bridge'. Time it with your guide for the receding tide, then stay for the sunset that follows: Neil's signature hour.

items.name: Laxmanpur Beach sunset, Neil Island
items.description: A long, west-facing sweep of shell-strewn sand that is the finest sunset perch on sleepy Neil, the Natural Bridge sits at its far end, so you pair the two into one unhurried evening. Neil's slower pace and empty beaches make it the antidote to busier Havelock.

items.name: Bharatpur Beach, Neil Island
items.description: Neil's shallow, swimmer-friendly lagoon right by the jetty, with soft coral close in and calm water, the island's water-sports beach for glass-bottom boats, snorkelling and easy swims. The gentlest sea in the region, well suited to children and nervous swimmers.

items.name: Sitapur Beach (Beach No. 1) sunrise, Neil Island
items.description: The easternmost beach on Neil, a natural little cove that catches the sunrise while the island is still asleep. Pair it with the Laxmanpur sunset and you bookend a full Neil day with the sea's two best moments.

items.name: Baratang, the limestone caves
items.description: A dawn convoy along the Andaman Trunk Road, then a speedboat through primeval mangrove creeks and a short forest walk to caves hung with stalactites and stalagmites, a proper adventure day out of Port Blair. The road crosses the protected Jarawa reserve in escorted convoy, where stopping, photography and any contact are strictly forbidden, and rightly so.

items.name: Baratang, the mud volcanoes
items.description: Small, bubbling cones of grey mud pushed up by natural gas, a rare geological curiosity and the other half of the classic Baratang day. Modest to look at but genuinely unusual, and a hit with children collecting oddities of nature.

items.name: Jolly Buoy Island, the marine national park
credentials: Within the Mahatma Gandhi Marine National Park (est. 1983)
Open seasonally (roughly Nov–Apr) on rotation with Red Skin to protect the reef
items.description: Inside the protected Mahatma Gandhi Marine National Park off Wandoor, Jolly Buoy is a strictly plastic-free island of untouched coral gardens seen by glass-bottom boat and snorkel. It opens only part of the year to let the reef recover, some of the most pristine, best-protected coral you can still swim over in India.

items.name: Red Skin Island, the marine national park
credentials: Within the Mahatma Gandhi Marine National Park
Open seasonally (roughly Mar–Sep) on rotation with Jolly Buoy
items.description: Jolly Buoy's counterpart in the same marine park, opening on the alternate season so the reefs are always rested, the same clear coral gardens, glass-bottom boats and snorkelling from a permit-controlled, single-use-plastic-free island. Whichever is open when you visit is the day-trip to book from Port Blair.

items.name: Diglipur, Ross & Smith twin islands
items.description: Far in the wild north, two islands joined by a dazzling white sandbar that appears and vanishes with the tide, so you can walk from one to the other across the sea. Remote, barely developed and staggeringly beautiful, the reward for those who go beyond the standard three-island circuit.

items.name: Saddle Peak, the archipelago's highest point
items.description: At 732 metres, the highest summit in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, reached by a demanding 8km forest trek through evergreen jungle to panoramic views over the north coast. A serious half-day hike for the fit and adventurous, and the roof of the islands.

items.name: Turtle nesting at Kalipur & Ramnagar beaches
items.description: The dark-sand beaches around Diglipur are among the few places on earth where four species of sea turtle, including the giant leatherback, come ashore to nest between roughly October and March. Guided night walks let you witness turtles laying and, later in the season, hatchlings scrambling to the sea: a quiet, unforgettable wildlife privilege.

items.name: Barren Island, India's only active volcano
items.description: A conical, smoking island rising from the sea 135km east of Port Blair, the only confirmed active volcano in South Asia, where black lava slopes meet electric-blue water. Landing is forbidden, but scenic boat and seaplane approaches, and world-class liveaboard dives over lava-formed reefs teeming with sharks and manta rays, make it a bucket-list expedition for serious divers.

items.name: Long Island & Guitar Island, the hidden Andamans
items.description: Reached by boat from Havelock, Long Island keeps its jungle village pace with barely a road, and a short hop away Guitar Island is a guitar-shaped sliver of sand that becomes a floating sandbar at high tide. This is the Andamans before tourism, empty beaches, silence, and the pleasure of a private-boat picnic with nobody else in sight.

items.name: Radhanagar Beach, Beach No. 5 sandbar walk
items.description: Just before Radhanagar proper, a natural lagoon and sandbar (locally 'Beach No. 5' or Neil's Cove) offers calm, shallow water ideal for a gentle swim away from the main beach's crowds. A quiet companion stop that most day-trippers miss.

items.name: The stilt-luxury of Taj Exotica, Radhanagar
items.description: The islands' flagship resort, 72 stilt villas with private plunge pools spread across rainforest and a private stretch by Radhanagar, styled on Nicobari and Jarawa architecture and built without felling a tree. Even non-guests can dine at a private beach table or spa at the J Wellness Circle; for a honeymoon or multi-gen escape it sets the bar for what tropical India can offer.

items.name: The Rajiv Gandhi Water Sports Complex, Aberdeen
items.description: On the Marina Park waterfront by Aberdeen Jetty, this is the launch point for Ross Island and North Bay and a cluster of jet-ski, banana-boat and speedboat rides over the harbour. A convenient, family-friendly first taste of the water before the outer islands, and the gateway jetty you will pass through more than once.

items.name: Discover-Scuba & the shore reef at Nemo Reef
items.description: For those who have never dived, a supervised Discover-Scuba session on Havelock takes complete beginners, no certification, minimum age around ten, down to shallow, sheltered coral to breathe underwater for the first time among clownfish and anemones. The gentle, hand-held introduction that turns a nervous first-timer into a diver by lunchtime.

items.name: Glass-bottom boat over the reef
items.description: The dry, effortless way for grandparents and small children to see live coral, fish and the occasional turtle, a flat-bottomed boat with a glass floor gliding over the reefs off North Bay or Elephant Beach. The inclusive option that lets a whole multi-generational group share the underwater world at once.

items.name: Jetty-hopping Havelock → Neil by private ferry
items.description: The two showcase islands sit a short catamaran-ferry apart, so a well-planned itinerary pairs Havelock's diving and Radhanagar with Neil's slower beaches and Natural Bridge in one seamless arc. A concierge who pre-books the fast ferries (they sell out in season) turns the region's fiddliest logistics into a smooth ribbon of island days.

items.name: The Settlers, Taj Exotica
credentials: Within Taj Exotica Resort & Spa, Andamans, the islands' only internationally-branded five-star kitchen
items.description: The resort's signature table, telling the Andamans' history through local ingredients, the most considered dinner on the islands.

items.name: Jalakara Restaurant
credentials: Within Jalakara, Condé Nast Traveller Gold List 2020 & Mr & Mrs Smith member hotel
items.description: A small, changing menu cooked with real intent in the jungle, dinner as a quiet, personal event rather than a service.

items.name: Barefoot Bar & Brasserie
credentials: Within Barefoot at Havelock, the Andamans' pioneering eco-resort
items.description: A thatched-hut dining room in the eco-original's forest, honest island cooking and fresh catch, barefoot and unhurried.

items.name: Full Moon Café
credentials: Long-standing Havelock traveller favourite, consistently among the island's highest-rated independent restaurants
items.description: A beach-facing bistro that has been Havelock's most-recommended independent table for years, fresh seafood, Indian and continental, done well.

items.name: Anju-Coco Resto
credentials: Well-known Havelock traveller favourite, noted for grilled tuna and attentive, personal service
items.description: A warm, family-run island favourite known for its grilled tuna and genuinely personal service, the honest heart of Havelock eating.

items.name: Something Different, A Beachside Café
credentials: Popular Havelock beachside café, a long-standing traveller favourite for its setting and seafood
items.description: Fusion seafood plates and a picture-perfect beach setting, the most scenic casual meal on the island.

items.name: Resort sundowner bars (Taj Exotica / Barefoot)
credentials: Within Taj Exotica Resort & Spa and Barefoot at Havelock, the islands' best-run bars
items.description: The most polished drink on the islands, a proper cocktail at sunset from the resort bars, which is as refined as an Andaman evening gets.

items.name: Beach-shack sundowners, Havelock
credentials: Havelock's informal beach-shack bars, the island's only real evening scene
items.description: The islands' idea of a night out, a cold drink and fresh grill at a beach shack as the sun goes down. That is the extent of it, honestly, and that is the point.

plan.heading: 5 days in the Andaman Islands, done well
plan.lede: A day-by-day shape for the trip, the pace we would set. Your advisor books the flights and the rooms; the days are yours.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: Fly into Port Blair, then transfer by private launch across the water to Havelock (Swaraj Dweep).

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: Settle into your villa at Taj Exotica Andamans on Radhanagar, the island's quiet western shore.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: Sundowners on Radhanagar Beach as the light goes, then dinner at the resort's overwater table.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: A guided dive or first-time discovery dive off Havelock's house reefs with a PADI instructor, the water warm and clear.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: Rest through the heat of the day, then a slow swim and reading hours on Radhanagar.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: Grilled catch of the day and a cold bottle of white on the sand.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: Private boat to Neil (Shaheed Dweep), calmer and greener, with a stop at the natural coral bridge at Laxmanpur.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: Snorkel the shallows off Bharatpur, then lunch under the casuarinas.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: Return to Havelock at dusk, an easy dinner at the villa.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: A dawn kayak through the mangrove creeks before the wind picks up, guide leading the way.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: A spa afternoon, or simply the hammock and the tide.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: A private dinner set on the beach, lanterns and the sound of the reef.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: Launch back to Port Blair; if time allows, a considered visit to the Cellular Jail before your flight.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: Depart Port Blair for the mainland.

items.name: Havelock (Swaraj Dweep)
items.description: The main island for beaches and diving with the better resorts; best for most travellers.

items.name: Neil (Shaheed Dweep)
items.description: The smaller, slower island of quiet coves; suits those wanting seclusion and calm.

items.name: Port Blair
items.description: The capital and transit hub with the historical sites; practical for arrival, less for a beach stay.

events.name: Island Tourism Festival
events.note: The islands' main cultural festival in Port Blair, with music, dance and craft from the archipelago's communities.

events.name: Peak diving & clear-water season
events.note: The dry season with the calmest seas and best visibility; the window to time a trip around the reefs.

events.name: Subhash Mela
events.note: A festival at the Cellular Jail marking Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose's birthday, tied to the islands' freedom history.

events.name: Monsoon (to avoid)
events.note: Heavy rain and rough seas disrupt ferries and diving; worth planning around by staying away.

onGround.heading: On the ground
onGround.note: No permit is needed for Indian passport holders, though restricted tribal areas are strictly off-limits; base yourself on Havelock (Taj or a private beach villa), factor ferry timings and monsoon season (May-September), and book diving at Radhanagar and Elephant Beach in advance.

rows.label: Arriving
rows.value: Fly into Port Blair (IXZ) via Chennai, Kolkata or Delhi, then a chauffeured car and, for Havelock, a private or premium ferry (or a seaplane-style charter) carries you on to the island resort.

rows.label: Getting around
rows.value: A private driver covers Port Blair, while on Havelock and Neil islands a resort car or hired jeep serves; boats handle all inter-island movement.

rows.label: Connectivity
rows.value: Mobile data is slow and patchy beyond Port Blair; the better resorts on Havelock offer wifi, but treat the islands as a place to disconnect.

rows.label: Money
rows.value: Indian rupee; carry ample cash as cards and ATMs are unreliable outside Port Blair; tipping boat crews and dive guides is customary.

rows.label: Climate
rows.value: November to April is the window, calm seas, 25 to 30°C, and the clearest water for diving, with January the settled peak. Avoid June to September, when the southwest monsoon roughens the sea, disrupts ferries and closes the outer islands.

rows.label: Flights from India
rows.value: Fly into Port Blair (IXZ, Veer Savarkar). Delhi has direct services (~3h40m) on Air India and IndiGo; from Mumbai and Bengaluru it is usually one connection via Chennai, Bengaluru or Kolkata (~5 to 6 hours total). No lie-flat first on the sector, so we arrange the Chennai/Bengaluru leg in business and a fast-track meet-and-greet at Port Blair, then a private seaplane or chartered boat onward to Havelock.

rows.label: Health & safety
rows.value: Domestic, no vaccinations required, though routine cover should be current. Islands are safe and calm; the real notes are practical, the sea, not crime. It is tropical, so mosquito-borne dengue/chikungunya rise in the wetter months; use repellent. Drink only bottled or filtered water, never the tap.

rows.label: Dining, veg & Jain
rows.value: Vegetarian is easy and Jain requests are honoured, but this is a remote island chain, Indian food leans simple South-Indian and Bengali rather than refined. The best kitchens are inside the resorts: Taj Exotica and Jalakara on Havelock both do a considered vegetarian and Jain menu with notice, which is the way to eat well here.
